notes: Context: fintech payments company, user-facing chat (support) + realtime reranking for offers. Very sensitive to latency spikes, financial impact on conversions.
Primary ask: dedicated GPU pool with clear throughput guarantees and latency SLOs defined for both streaming and non-streaming traffic.
SLO draft (customer wants alignment across client/server):
- Non-streaming (batch request -> single response): p50 <= 180ms, p95 <= 420ms, p99 <= 900ms (end-to-end client observed)
- Streaming (chat): time-to-first-token p50 <= 180ms, token-to-token steady-state p95 <= 30ms, end-of-stream p99 <= 1s (for short responses)
Measurement definitions — proposed alignment notes:
- Client-side timing = full end-to-end (DNS+TLS+client-queue+request+server-process+TLS-overhead+first/last byte). Ceres will report client telemetry (CDN/edge included).
- Server-side timing (Redwood) = time from request-received-at-edge -> last-token-emitted. Redwood to provide per-request server timing and granular per-token deltas for streaming.
- Correlation: require a trace-id in header for 100% of test traffic; both sides to store traces for post-mortem. Agree on name/format: X-Trace-Id.
- Measurement windows: 5-minute rolling windows for realtime SLO evaluation; daily rolling for SLA billing. Tail violations computed on p99 over 24h rolling.
Sampling & instrumentation:
- Synthetic harness: we will run 72h continuous synthetic tests replicating production prompt mix (20% long-form, 60% chat short, 20% embeddings/rerank).
- Production sampling: 1 in 50 requests instrumented for full-trace collection to correlate client vs server latency.
Reserved GPU planning notes:
- Baseline load: 1200 active concurrent users at peak -> estimated 180 RPS overall (mix weighted).
- Initial reserved sizing proposal: 4x A100-class GPUs (dedicated pool) with autoscale buffer of +25% burst capacity. Rationale: throughput headroom for quantized models and batched workloads.
- Concurrency model: prefer request-based concurrency limits (max inflight per-GPU) + dynamic batching to preserve p95 targets. We discussed max batch size = 8 for chat path.
SLA negotiation points (to close):
- Breach definition: end-to-end client p95/p99 misses vs server p95/p99 misses; want a joint view before applying credits.
- Credits: propose 10% monthly credit for >3 sustained p99 breaches in a 30d window; legal wants clearer measurement boundaries (edge vs client).
- Availability: 99.95% for dedicated pool, want escalation path for multi-hour incidents and a named PS contact.
Open technical asks from SEs:
- Validate per-token latency export for streaming (we can emit token timestamps via websocket events).
- Confirm how Redwood handles KV-cache warmup across model pins and canary rollouts — warmup impacts first-token latency.
Actionable next items (choppy):
- Redwood: provide 72h synthetic harness config + initial reserved sizing doc (by 2026-03-12).
- Ceres: share production request distribution and representative prompt set (by 2026-03-14).
- Legal/procurement: review SLA credit language; target procurement signature in May 2026.
Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- 'We need a joint SLO definition — blameless measurement; if client edge adds 300ms, credits shouldn't automatically apply to Redwood.'
- 'Streaming quality is a hard sell to operations — if first-token is slow it's worse than steady-state slow tokens.'
Risks noted:
- Data residency for EU merchants: need documentation and possibly a mirrored private deployment in eu-west region.
- Short-term tail events during canary deploys — recommend canary rate-limits + pre-warm flows.
Summary: customer is advanced, committed to dedicated if SLO measurement and reserved sizing are watertight. Next milestone is synthetic 72h tail test and legal SLA language.
